seeds.ex: Reading the first INVITE. The first INVITE has a magic-cookie branch, Max-Forwards 70, a From tag, and no To tag.
seeds.eg: Dissect a debug INVITE The capture bench strips the debug prefix. Read the branch and the missing To tag.

seeds.ti: The hitchhiker guide is a map
seeds.ex: The hitchhiker guide is a map. RFC 5411 is an informational map of the SIP document set, and it does not replace the base specification.
seeds.eg: Name the document On the 180, decide which RFC you would open if the response also contained Require: 100rel.

seeds.ti: Licenses, codecs, and what you may copy
seeds.ex: Licenses, codecs, and what you may copy. Protocol text is under the IETF trust provisions, and codec rights have to be read from the codec's own documents.
seeds.eg: Name the codec document The offer uses static payload 0. Identify which recommendation defines that codec.

seeds.ti: Ports, transports, and where a request can go
seeds.ex: Ports, transports, and where a request can go. SIP uses UDP or TCP on 5060 and TLS on 5061, and a request that does not fit one datagram needs a connection.
seeds.eg: Read the OPTIONS Dissect the OPTIONS. The CSeq method token has to match the request line.

seeds.ex: Dialog identity. A dialog is identified by Call-ID, the From tag, and the To tag, and the initial request has no To tag.
seeds.eg: Find the dialog id Dissect the 180. List the three values that identify the early dialog.

seeds.ex: Headers and compact forms. Compact header names are aliases from RFC 3261, with a few more aliases defined in the extension RFCs.
seeds.eg: Rewrite From on purpose Run the profile. It is legal syntax and a dangerous edit. See which URI the From header contains afterward.

seeds.ex: Methods and status codes. The core methods are INVITE, ACK, OPTIONS, BYE, CANCEL, and REGISTER, and status codes fall into six classes.
seeds.eg: Class the code Dissect the final response in this lab message, which is the 486.

seeds.ti: Roles a trace is actually showing
seeds.ex: Roles a trace is actually showing. A trace shows a user agent, a proxy, a registrar, a redirect server, or a B2BUA, and products often combine those roles.
seeds.eg: Who is still on the ladder? After the ACK of the 302, which role is finished?

seeds.ti: T1, the transaction timeout, and Timer C
seeds.ex: T1, the transaction timeout, and Timer C. T1 seeds retransmissions, 64 times T1 ends the transaction, and Timer C is the proxy's longer INVITE arm.
seeds.eg: Count the gaps The second and third arrows are retransmissions. State the first Timer A value.

seeds.ex: Transactions and the branch cookie. A transaction is identified by the branch, and a retransmission repeats that branch instead of starting a new one.
seeds.eg: Compare the two branches Inspect the retransmitted INVITE and the ACK. Decide which hop starts a new transaction.

seeds.ex: CANCEL, BYE, and re-INVITE. CANCEL abandons an unanswered INVITE, BYE ends a confirmed dialog, and re-INVITE changes a dialog that already exists.
seeds.eg: Dissect a BYE This BYE assumes the dialog already exists. Find the CSeq and the To tag.

seeds.ex: PRACK and reliable provisionals. A provisional response with Require: 100rel is retransmitted until PRACK, and RAck names that exact response.
seeds.eg: Check RAck Dissect the PRACK. Separate RAck from CSeq.

seeds.ex: Record-Route and the route set. A proxy that wants to stay on the dialog prepends a Record-Route URI, and that URI has to contain lr.
seeds.eg: Put lr back The header-rule matches a Record-Route that lost lr and writes the parameter back.

seeds.ex: REFER and Replaces. REFER asks another UA to send a request, and Replaces names the dialog that request should take over.
seeds.eg: Read Refer-To Find the Replaces parameter inside Refer-To. It is escaped.

seeds.ex: Session-Expires and 422. Session timers name who refreshes the dialog, and 422 tells the caller the interval was below Min-SE.
seeds.eg: Read the 422 The response tells you the floor. The next INVITE has to meet it.

seeds.ex: UPDATE before the INVITE completes. UPDATE can change the session while the initial INVITE is still outstanding, and it does not use the ACK rules.
seeds.eg: Negotiate the second offer The UPDATE offer adds a port change and still lists PCMU and PCMA. The answer keeps PCMU.

seeds.ex: Locating a server with RFC 3263. RFC 3263 turns a SIP domain into a transport, a port, and an address with NAPTR, SRV, and A or AAAA.
seeds.eg: What happened before the INVITE The first note states the DNS result. The SIP itself contains no NAPTR records.

seeds.ex: Forking and early dialogs. A forking proxy creates one client transaction per binding, and each To tag is a separate early dialog.
seeds.eg: Separate the tags Step both 180 responses. The Call-ID matches and the To tags do not.

seeds.ex: GRUU and a single instance. A GRUU routes to one UA instance, and the registrar returns it as pub-gruu or temp-gruu on the binding.
seeds.eg: Find both GRUUs The 200 OK Contact carries pub-gruu and temp-gruu.

seeds.ex: Loose routing and Max-Forwards. With lr, the Request-URI stays the remote target, each hop pops its own Route, and Max-Forwards of 0 yields 483.
seeds.eg: Watch Route shrink Compare the Route headers on the first and second BYE.

seeds.ex: Outbound, reg-id, and keepalives. RFC 5626 binds a UA instance to one or more flows with reg-id and +sip.instance, and keepalives hold those flows open.
seeds.eg: Count the flows Dissect the second 200 OK. Two Contact headers share an instance and differ by reg-id.

seeds.ex: Path and Service-Route. Path is the inbound vector stored with a binding, and Service-Route is the outbound vector the registrar gives the UA.
seeds.eg: Which header is outbound? The 200 OK has both Path and Service-Route. Pick the one the UA will preload.

seeds.ex: REGISTER and bindings. REGISTER binds an address-of-record to one or more Contacts, and the registrar is a different role from the proxy.
seeds.eg: Read the 423 The registrar rejected the interval. The header you need is Min-Expires.

seeds.ex: Direction attributes and hold. sendrecv, sendonly, recvonly, and inactive are per stream. Hold is commonly sendonly or inactive.
seeds.eg: Answer a hold The offer is sendonly. A legal answer is recvonly. Negotiate and read the direction line.

seeds.ex: Early media and 183. 183 Session Progress with SDP is the usual early-media pattern. 180 means ringing. A 183 does not always have SDP.
seeds.eg: 183 has SDP, 180 does not Extract both responses. One progress message has SDP and the ringing message does not.

seeds.ex: Offer/answer pitfalls in RFC 6337. RFC 6337 is the usage document for offer/answer mistakes: order, version, delayed offer, and hold.
seeds.eg: Find the delayed offer This INVITE has an empty body. Decide where the offer is allowed to appear.

seeds.ex: Port 0 rejects a stream. Port 0 refuses the stream in that slot. The m-line stays, with a protocol and a format list.
seeds.eg: See a zero port Negotiate an offer of two audio lines. The answer accepts the first and zeros the second.

seeds.ex: rtpmap names and fmtp parameters. Match codecs by the rtpmap encoding name. The G.722 rtpmap clock stays 8000.
seeds.eg: Match opus on the name The offer says payload 96 opus. The answer says payload 111 opus. G722/8000 is on payload 9 on both sides.

seeds.ex: Static and dynamic payload types. RFC 3551 assigns static payload types. Dynamic types are named by rtpmap, and G.722 stays at clock 8000.
seeds.eg: Read static types The offer lists PCMU and PCMA on separate m-lines. Confirm the clocks are 8000.

seeds.ex: ptime, packet rate, and EF. ptime is SDP. Twenty milliseconds of G.711 is 50 packets per second and 160 bytes of payload, plus headers. Voice sits in the EF class.
seeds.eg: Read ptime 20 Both sides show a=ptime:20 and PCMU/8000. Compute packets per second and payload bytes.

seeds.ex: RTCP sender and receiver reports. RTCP sender reports and receiver reports describe the RTP flow. A SIP 200 OK does not report loss.
seeds.eg: Name the RTCP port The answer says m=audio 40030. Apply the RFC 3550 default and name the RTCP port.

seeds.ex: telephone-event and other digit paths. telephone-event is RFC 4733, a dynamic payload. Events 0 through 15 are DTMF. INFO and KPML are different tools.
seeds.eg: Negotiate telephone-event The offer uses payload 101 and the answer uses payload 106. Both rtpmap lines say telephone-event/8000 and fmtp lists 0-15.

seeds.ex: Privacy and asserted identity. Privacy is RFC 3323. P-Asserted-Identity and P-Preferred-Identity are for trusted networks, not cryptographic identity.
seeds.eg: See PAI on the wrong hop This INVITE is addressed to the carrier and still contains P-Asserted-Identity and Privacy: id.

seeds.ex: SRTP and two keying methods. SRTP is RFC 3711. SDES a=crypto is RFC 4568. DTLS-SRTP is RFC 5764. An SBC must not assume peers share one method.
seeds.eg: See the profile mismatch The offer is RTP/SAVP. The answer is RTP/AVP. Negotiate and read the profile warning.

seeds.ex: STIR, PASSporT, and SHAKEN. STIR is RFC 8224, PASSporT is RFC 8225, certificates are RFC 8226, and the SHAKEN extension is RFC 8588. Attestation levels are ATIS.
seeds.eg: No Identity header Dissect the INVITE. Decide whether it is STIR-authenticated.

seeds.ex: Scanning, hijack, and toll fraud. Scanning, registration hijack, and toll fraud are classes of abuse. The response is authentication, exposure control, and alerting.
seeds.eg: Read an unchallenged REGISTER result Dissect the 200 OK. The Contact is 192.0.2.40 and there was no digest challenge.

seeds.ex: TLS and domain certificates. SIP over TLS is RFC 3261 section 18. The certificate has to identify the SIP domain, per RFC 5922.
seeds.eg: Read a TLS Via Dissect the INVITE. The transport is TLS. The domain in the request is example.com.

seeds.ex: Media latching on an SBC. Many SBCs learn the remote RTP address from the first packet instead of trusting c=. That is deployment practice, and RFC 5853 is the requirements RFC.
seeds.eg: Compare c= with the packet source Extract the INVITE and read c=. Then read the RTP note. The source port's address is not the c= address.

seeds.ex: Embedded addresses and NAT. SIP and SDP embed IP addresses. NAT rewrites the packet header and leaves those embedded addresses behind.
seeds.eg: Read a routable c= line Dissect the offer. c= uses the documentation address 203.0.113.10. The fault beside this lab is the private-address case.

seeds.ex: rport and symmetric responses. RFC 3581 adds rport so the response is sent to the source address and port the request came from.
seeds.eg: Read rport on the response Dissect the 100 Trying. Via has received and rport filled in.

seeds.ex: STUN server-reflexive addresses. STUN, RFC 8489, lets a client learn the address a server sees. It obsoletes RFC 5389.
seeds.eg: Separate STUN text from SIP The capture has a STUN note and a SIP 200 OK. Only one of them is a Binding result.

seeds.ti: Call admission stays on the datasheet
seeds.ex: Call admission stays on the datasheet. An SBC can refuse a new INVITE when its configured budget is exhausted. The number itself is platform-specific.
seeds.eg: Read the refusal Step the ladder. Which response refuses the call?

seeds.ti: An SBC is commonly a B2BUA
seeds.ex: An SBC is commonly a B2BUA. RFC 7092 taxonomizes B2BUAs. An SBC is commonly a UAS on one side and a UAC on the other, not a pure proxy.
seeds.eg: Dissect the outbound INVITE This is the SBC’s outbound INVITE. Which Call-ID belongs to the carrier leg?

seeds.ti: Active and standby, without a made-up timer
seeds.ex: Active and standby, without a made-up timer. Active/standby is a product behavior. One unit owns the work and the other is ready. Timers belong in that product’s HA guide.
seeds.eg: Count the SIP hops Play the call. How many SIP roles does the standby occupy in the ladder?

seeds.ex: Anchor, bypass, transcode, and DTMF. Anchoring terminates RTP on the SBC. Bypass lets endpoints exchange media. Transcoding and DTMF interworking need the media path.
seeds.eg: Negotiate an anchored answer Alice offers PCMU and PCMA. The anchored answer keeps PCMU and telephone-event.

seeds.ex: OPTIONS keepalives. SBCs probe a peer with OPTIONS. A 200 OK means the peer answered. The interval is product configuration.
seeds.eg: Check the OPTIONS CSeq Dissect this keepalive. What is the CSeq method?

seeds.ti: RFC 5853 is requirements, not a protocol
seeds.ex: RFC 5853 is requirements, not a protocol. RFC 5853 collects requirements from SBC deployments. It does not define an SBC wire protocol.
seeds.eg: Find the protocol Play the ladder. Which start line is an SBC-specific method?

seeds.ti: Topology hiding rewrites the addresses you leak
seeds.ex: Topology hiding rewrites the addresses you leak. Topology hiding replaces caller addresses in signaling and, when media is anchored, in SDP.
seeds.eg: Compare Contact hosts Dissect the carrier INVITE. Which host is in Contact?

seeds.ti: CUCM trunks, SIP profiles, and Lua
seeds.ex: CUCM trunks, SIP profiles, and Lua. A CUCM SIP trunk and a CUCM SIP profile are not the CUBE voice class. Lua normalization scripts exist. MTP required is version-specific.
seeds.eg: Dissect the trunk INVITE This INVITE leaves CUCM toward CUBE. Which host is in Contact?

seeds.ex: debug ccsip messages. debug ccsip messages displays sent and received SIP. Profile decisions have a separate debug, and the analyzer can test a profile offline.
seeds.eg: Parse a synthetic debug This is synthetic debug ccsip messages output. Separate Received from Sent.

seeds.ex: Early offer and delayed offer. Delayed offer means the INVITE has no SDP. voice-class sip early-offer forced makes the outbound dial peer send an offer in the INVITE.
seeds.eg: Read the forced offer The outbound early offer is ANCHOR_SDP. The carrier answer is CARRIER_SDP.

seeds.ex: voice class sip-profiles. A voice class sip-profiles rule can add, modify, or remove a header on a named method. Inbound support arrived after Cisco IOS 15.4.
seeds.eg: Remove Diversion Run the CUBE subset rule against the inbound INVITE. Diversion should disappear.

seeds.ex: Unity Connection SIP integration. SIP integration with CUCM is the documented Unity Connection path. Open the guide for your version. This lesson does not make SCCP the default.
seeds.eg: Find the called number Dissect the forwarded INVITE. Which header carries +15551212 as the redirecting target?

seeds.ex: Header rules run in order. Oracle HMR header rules run in configured order. The 10.1 fundamentals page names add, delete, manipulate, store, and reject.
seeds.eg: Delete Server Run this Acme header-rule subset against the INVITE. Server should disappear.

seeds.ex: AudioCodes manipulation in software 7.6. Software 7.6 message manipulation is a table of Message Type, Condition, Action Subject, Action Type, and Action Value, assigned to an IP group.
seeds.eg: Read one 7.6 row Which column contains Remove?

seeds.ex: Certificate names and Contact. The certificate name and the SIP Contact need to be names the peer accepts. Teams and Webex Local Gateway do not share a wildcard rule.
seeds.eg: Read the Teams Contact Dissect the TLS INVITE. Is Contact an FQDN or an IP?

seeds.ex: Three manipulation grammars. CUBE, Oracle HMR, and AudioCodes 7.6 can each remove a header. The grammars are not interchangeable.
seeds.eg: Identify the row Three fragments are printed. Which one is the AudioCodes 7.6 action?

seeds.ex: Oracle SBC objects. Oracle Communications SBC, formerly Acme Packet, is configured with realms, interfaces, session agents, and manipulation objects.
seeds.eg: Name the attachment These are documentation object names. Which one selects manipulation for messages leaving?

seeds.ex: Identity at a trust boundary. P-Asserted-Identity is a network-asserted identity. An SBC at a trust boundary decides whether that assertion continues.
seeds.eg: Find the assertion Dissect the carrier INVITE. Which header asserts the identity?

seeds.ti: Ribbon Edge, Core, and public validation lists
seeds.ex: Ribbon Edge, Core, and public validation lists. SBC SWe Edge shares a software family with SBC 1000 and SBC 2000. SBC Core is a separate family. Admin guides and interop guides are the sources for procedures.
seeds.eg: Keep the families apart Play the call. Which SIP method names the Ribbon family?

seeds.ex: Amazon Connect voice boundaries. Ordinary Connect calls use managed PSTN. SIPREC can feed a conversational analytics connector. A carrier bridged through Voice Connector is not the supported pattern.
seeds.eg: Name the recording relationship Dissect the synthetic SIPREC INVITE. Which address is the Request-URI host?

seeds.ti: Five9 BYO SIP and Twilio trunks
seeds.ex: Five9 BYO SIP and Twilio trunks. Five9 BYO SIP connects your ITSP or gateway to Five9 SBCs. Twilio termination and origination are different directions, with a strict Request-URI rule.
seeds.eg: Read the termination Request-URI The termination URI host in this lab is sbc1.example.com. What host does this INVITE use?

seeds.ti: Genesys BYOC and NICE CXone SIP
seeds.ex: Genesys BYOC and NICE CXone SIP. BYOC Cloud and BYOC Premises can be combined. NICE CXone documents SIP trunks on 5060 and 5061 with dynamic RTP and SRTP. Confirm carrier details with NICE.
seeds.eg: Whose date is it? Play the BYOC Cloud ladder, then answer from the Premises article rather than from the SIP itself.

seeds.ex: OPTIONS health and SRTP media. OPTIONS followed by 200 marks the SBC healthy. Media processors use SRTP. The protocol article’s OPTIONS CSeq cell disagrees with RFC 3261.
seeds.eg: Dissect a legal OPTIONS This is the request to send. What is the CSeq method?

seeds.ex: Teams Direct Routing signaling. Direct Routing uses the pstnhub proxies on 5061, a certified SBC, and a verified domain. Contact must be an FQDN.
seeds.eg: Check Contact and the proxy host Dissect the Direct Routing INVITE. Which host is in Contact?

seeds.ex: Webex Calling Local Gateway. An IOS XE Local Gateway uses SIP TLS and SRTP. Third-party SBCs use a certificate-based trunk. Wildcard certificates are not supported. ByoPSTN means bring your own PSTN.
seeds.eg: Read the Local Gateway offer The Local Gateway offer is SRTP. Which transport is in the m= line?

seeds.ti: Three PSTN choices, one per location
seeds.ex: Three PSTN choices, one per location. Webex Calling offers Cisco Calling Plan, Cloud Connected PSTN, or premises-based PSTN through a Local Gateway. A location has one PSTN connection.
seeds.eg: Name this ladder Step the call. Which PSTN model is on the wire here?

seeds.ti: Read an RFC header before you cite it
seeds.ex: Read an RFC header before you cite it. Number, category, and Obsoletes or Updates. The RFC Editor header beats a remembered month.
seeds.eg: Name the SDP RFC on the offer Inspect the first INVITE body. Which RFC number does this lesson use for SDP now?

seeds.ex: IOS ccsip and ccapi debug. debug ccsip messages prints SIP on IOS voice. debug voip ccapi inout prints call-control API output, which is not a SIP RFC.
seeds.eg: Dissect the SIP inside the debug The message below is what a synthetic debug ccsip messages capture would contain after the IOS prefix. debug voip ccapi inout is a different IOS command and is not this text.

seeds.ex: 488 codecs and 422 session timers. 488 is this UA refusing the session description. 422 is a session interval below Min-SE.
seeds.eg: See the overlap Negotiate this synthetic offer and answer. PCMU and telephone-event are on both sides. PCMA is only in the offer.

seeds.ti: Match a ladder before you change anything
seeds.ex: Match a ladder before you change anything. A ladder is one dialog only after Call-ID, CSeq, the Via branch, and the To tag agree.
seeds.eg: Find the end-to-end ACK Play the ladder. Which hop is the ACK for the 200 OK, and which branch does it use?

seeds.ti: Status codes you will actually see
seeds.ex: Status codes you will actually see. Read provisional and final codes from RFC 3261 section 21, and keep 422 with RFC 4028.
seeds.eg: Name the 487 Step the ladder. Which response ends the INVITE, and which 200 belongs to the CANCEL?

seeds.ti: TLS names, trust anchors, and version
seeds.ex: TLS names, trust anchors, and version. Handshake failures stay below SIP. A Teams 403 is the Contact FQDN rule after TLS is up.
seeds.eg: Find the FQDN Inspect the INVITE Contact. What hostname is in it, and what would a bare address draw?

seeds.ti: Display filters for SIP and RTP
seeds.ex: Display filters for SIP and RTP. Filter the capture with sip, rtp, and sip.Method, and confirm sip.CSeq.method in the SIP display-filter reference.
seeds.eg: Extract the INVITE from a text capture This is a synthetic text capture, not a customer packet. Extract the SIP message. On a real file you would display-filter with sip, and you would confirm sip.CSeq.method == "INVITE" in the Wireshark SIP display-filter reference.

seeds.ex: Alarms that match the failure. Alarm on OPTIONS, TLS expiry, 503, recording-session failure, and trusted-list rejects. Each alarm names its document.
seeds.eg: Read the 503 What status did the carrier return to OPTIONS, and what class of alarm is it?

seeds.ex: One change in the window. Freeze the baseline, change one variable, verify, and keep the previous snippet ready.
seeds.eg: Count the variables Between the baseline OPTIONS and the INVITE, how many variables did the lesson change?

seeds.ti: Emergency calling, location, and the FCC page
seeds.ex: Emergency calling, location, and the FCC page. Service URN, location conveyance, and the FCC MLTS page. State PSAP rules are not invented here.
seeds.eg: Read the Request-URI Inspect the first INVITE. What is the Request-URI?

seeds.ex: The toll-fraud class, stated defensively. Four exposure classes, source restrictions, and caller-identity as a separate control.
seeds.eg: Name the listed source Which source address on the first hop is the listed call agent?

seeds.ti: Voice, EF, and what the PHB does not design
seeds.ex: Voice, EF, and what the PHB does not design. RFC 3246 defines the EF PHB. RFC 4594 maps telephony to EF. This lesson does not design a LAN.
seeds.eg: Where EF applies Which hop's SDP names the media that the telephony class covers?

seeds.ex: Disclosed recording with SIPREC. RFC 7866 is the recording protocol. RFC 7865 is the metadata. Notice and retention are legal questions.
seeds.eg: Separate the two Call-IDs Which Call-ID belongs to the recording session toward the SRS?

seeds.ex: Trusted addresses and source restrictions. The IP address trusted list is per product page. CME and SRST do not share one list size.
seeds.eg: Trusted list teaching snippet Read the snippet. It is the CME pattern for a border that trusts the call agent and the carrier. SRST uses its own page. No list size is stated.

seeds.ex: Certifications this edition will name. SSCA, CCNP Collaboration, and MS-721, with the dates this edition actually checked. Other vendor exam codes stay unconfirmed.
seeds.eg: Cite the ACK the exams share The last hop is the ACK for 200 OK. Which documents cover it?

seeds.ti: Webex Calling local gateway, and a separate contact center
seeds.ex: Webex Calling local gateway, and a separate contact center. Premises PSTN for Webex Calling uses Local Gateway. Webex Contact Center is a separate product with its own design guide.
seeds.eg: Name the pattern Which product's premises-PSTN pattern is this ladder?

seeds.ti: A glossary tied to a document
seeds.ex: A glossary tied to a document. Every term in your notes points at a role and a document, not at a product logo.
seeds.eg: Name the outbound role On the outbound INVITE, which role do you write if this SBC is a B2BUA?

seeds.ti: Neighbors that are not SIP elements
seeds.ex: Neighbors that are not SIP elements. WFM and QM are operations systems. CRM is not a SIP element. Recording, location, and the media path keep their real documents.
seeds.eg: Keep CRM off the arrow Which party list would wrongly add a CRM as a SIP hop?

seeds.ti: When the page and the memory disagree
seeds.ex: When the page and the memory disagree. The RFC Editor banner, the Cisco exam page, and the Microsoft certification page outrank a remembered line.
seeds.eg: Who wins on SDP The offer is SDP. Which number do you cite when a blog still says 4566 is current?

seeds.ti: CUCM, UCCX, and CVP without a fake script
seeds.ex: CUCM, UCCX, and CVP without a fake script. CUCM is the call-control point. UCCX rides on CUCM. CVP's SIP paths are in the guide for the version you run.
seeds.eg: Where the carrier INVITE stops first The first hop is the carrier. Which element receives it?

seeds.ti: Workforce tools and agents above the media
seeds.ex: Workforce tools and agents above the media. Agents and workforce tools sit above the media path. The session is still SIP, and the voice is still RTP.
seeds.eg: Point at the media hop Which response carries the answer that lets RTP start?

seeds.ti: An interconnect checklist, not a config dump
seeds.ex: An interconnect checklist, not a config dump. Record TLS, codecs including telephone-event, E.164, trusted addresses, OPTIONS, and the SRTP keying choice.
seeds.eg: Find two rows on the INVITE The INVITE hop carries a number and an offer. Which checklist rows are those?

seeds.ti: CUCM, a certified SBC, and Teams Direct Routing
seeds.ex: CUCM, a certified SBC, and Teams Direct Routing. CUBE or another certified SBC can sit between CUCM and Teams. No architecture SKU is invented here.
seeds.eg: Read Contact on the Teams INVITE What does Contact contain on the hop toward Teams?

seeds.ti: Media drill with the cited answer
seeds.ex: Media drill with the cited answer. 488, 422, telephone-event, RTP, and the SRTP keying choice, each answered in the prose.
seeds.eg: Name this 488 The final response is 488. What do you say in the interview?

seeds.ti: SBC drill with the cited answer
seeds.ex: SBC drill with the cited answer. B2BUA, where PSTN SIP lands, the trusted list, and Teams TLS, answered in the body.
seeds.eg: Count the legs How do you match the carrier 200 to the caller's ACK?

seeds.ti: Signaling drill with the cited answer
seeds.ex: Signaling drill with the cited answer. Each signaling answer is written here, with the RFC, before the quiz asks it.
seeds.eg: Say the ACK kind The last hop follows 200 OK. What kind of ACK is it?

seeds.ti: Symptom, ladder, one packet, one variable
seeds.ex: Symptom, ladder, one packet, one variable. The sequence is symptom, ladder, one packet, change one variable. The log in this lesson is synthetic.
seeds.eg: Pick the one packet Which hop is the packet the method allows you to act on before you change config?

seeds.ex: Browser softphone call flow. A study ladder: WebSocket handshake, SIP INVITE, answer, then DTLS on the media path. Step the hops.
seeds.eg: Step the softphone ladder Play or step. Stop on DTLS and say which path it uses.

seeds.ti: DTLS-SRTP and the required audio codecs
seeds.ex: DTLS-SRTP and the required audio codecs. WebRTC media is SRTP. The profile is RTP/SAVPF. Opus, PCMA, and PCMU are required audio codecs.
seeds.eg: Read the offer proto and the Opus line The offer uses UDP/TLS/RTP/SAVPF and names opus/48000/2. The answer keeps Opus.

seeds.ti: Signaling, JSEP, and the media plane
seeds.ex: Signaling, JSEP, and the media plane. WebRTC names a browser protocol suite. JSEP leaves the signaling protocol to the application. SIP over WebSocket is one such protocol.
seeds.eg: Name the document Step the ladder. The first hop is an HTTP handshake. The third hop is SIP.

seeds.ex: Asterisk, PJSIP, and the dialplan. chan_pjsip is the SIP channel driver. res_pjsip reads pjsip.conf. extensions.conf is the dialplan. The license page is GPL version 2, with a stated exception for AMI, AGI, and ARI.
seeds.eg: Which file A study sketch with the file names from the docs. It is not a working endpoint.

seeds.ex: FreeSWITCH profiles, dialplan, and WebRTC. The manual covers SIP profiles, the dialplan, codecs, media, WebRTC, and the Event Socket. There is an open source edition and an enterprise edition.
seeds.eg: Separate the products Three names from the page. Pick the open source build.

seeds.ex: Kamailio as the SIP server. Kamailio is an open source SIP server under GPLv2+. Its page lists proxy, registrar, WebSocket, and scaling in front of a PBX.
seeds.eg: Who answers the dialplan Kamailio received the INVITE. Asterisk is the next hop.

seeds.ex: rtpengine and the integration map. rtpengine proxies RTP, rewrites SDP, and can bridge ICE and SRTP. It runs on GNU/Linux and is meant to sit with Kamailio.
seeds.eg: Read the rewritten c= line The offer points at the phone. The answer points at the proxy. That is the anchoring idea.

seeds.ex: Troubleshooting without a legal conclusion. Sort the symptom into SIP, identity, emergency location, or messaging. Then open that document. Educational only. Not legal advice.
seeds.eg: Pick the next document One symptom. One next document. No legal conclusion.

seeds.ex: 10DLC is a messaging channel. The Campaign Registry describes 10DLC as an A2P messaging channel with verified brands and campaign service providers. It is not SIP. Educational only.
seeds.eg: Split the ticket Two symptoms arrived in one ticket. Separate them.

seeds.ti: Bridges from enterprise UC to open platforms
seeds.ex: Bridges from enterprise UC to open platforms. CUCM, Webex, and the contact center already have SIP seams in this lab. The open projects are the other side of a trunk, not a hidden mode inside CUCM.
seeds.eg: Name both sides A trunk is up. Name the object on each side without merging the names.

seeds.ex: Configuration and troubleshooting seams. Configure the file the project names. Troubleshoot the plane that failed. Do not copy a sample this lab did not print.
seeds.eg: Choose the file The endpoint exists. The extension 1000 does not ring. Asterisk is the PBX.

seeds.ti: Integration hooks that are already named
seeds.ex: Integration hooks that are already named. Future work should use hooks the documents already name: AMI, AGI, ARI, the Event Socket, SIPREC, and SIP over WebSocket. This lab does not ship a live connector.
seeds.eg: Pick a real hook You want a program to hear that an Asterisk call is ringing. Choose an interface the license page names.

seeds.ex: Sister technologies around the session. WFM, recording, emergency policy, analytics, CRM, AI agents, and programmable APIs hang off the session. They are not SIP proxies.
seeds.eg: Name the neighbor The symptom is a recording that never starts. SIP to the phone works.

seeds.ex: Browser softphone call flow. A study ladder: WebSocket handshake, SIP INVITE, answer, then DTLS on the media path. Step the hops.
seeds.eg: Step the softphone ladder Play or step. Stop on DTLS and say which path it uses.

docs.ti: E.164, sip URIs, and tel URIs
docs.ex: E.164, sip URIs, and tel URIs. A global number is written in a tel URI or in a sip URI user part, and E.164 is the numbering plan those digits follow.
docs.eg: Dissect the phone URI Find the URI parameter that marks the user part as a phone number.

docs.ex: Reading the first INVITE. The first INVITE has a magic-cookie branch, Max-Forwards 70, a From tag, and no To tag.
docs.eg: Dissect a debug INVITE The capture bench strips the debug prefix. Read the branch and the missing To tag.

docs.ti: The hitchhiker guide is a map
docs.ex: The hitchhiker guide is a map. RFC 5411 is an informational map of the SIP document set, and it does not replace the base specification.
docs.eg: Name the document On the 180, decide which RFC you would open if the response also contained Require: 100rel.

docs.ti: Licenses, codecs, and what you may copy
docs.ex: Licenses, codecs, and what you may copy. Protocol text is under the IETF trust provisions, and codec rights have to be read from the codec's own documents.
docs.eg: Name the codec document The offer uses static payload 0. Identify which recommendation defines that codec.

docs.ti: Ports, transports, and where a request can go
docs.ex: Ports, transports, and where a request can go. SIP uses UDP or TCP on 5060 and TLS on 5061, and a request that does not fit one datagram needs a connection.
docs.eg: Read the OPTIONS Dissect the OPTIONS. The CSeq method token has to match the request line.

docs.ex: How to read an RFC. A SIP argument cites the RFC number and the section, and the normative sentences outrank a broken example.
docs.eg: Point at the chapter Step the ladder. For the ACK, name the fact that separates it from the INVITE transaction.

docs.ex: What SIP is for. SIP creates, changes, and ends sessions, while RTP carries the media those sessions describe.
docs.eg: Find the offer Play the ladder and open the first INVITE. The audio offer is the SDP body, not a later response.

docs.ex: Dialog identity. A dialog is identified by Call-ID, the From tag, and the To tag, and the initial request has no To tag.
docs.eg: Find the dialog id Dissect the 180. List the three values that identify the early dialog.

docs.ex: Headers and compact forms. Compact header names are aliases from RFC 3261, with a few more aliases defined in the extension RFCs.
docs.eg: Rewrite From on purpose Run the profile. It is legal syntax and a dangerous edit. See which URI the From header contains afterward.

docs.ex: Methods and status codes. The core methods are INVITE, ACK, OPTIONS, BYE, CANCEL, and REGISTER, and status codes fall into six classes.
docs.eg: Class the code Dissect the final response in this lab message, which is the 486.

docs.ti: Roles a trace is actually showing
docs.ex: Roles a trace is actually showing. A trace shows a user agent, a proxy, a registrar, a redirect server, or a B2BUA, and products often combine those roles.
docs.eg: Who is still on the ladder? After the ACK of the 302, which role is finished?

docs.ti: T1, the transaction timeout, and Timer C
docs.ex: T1, the transaction timeout, and Timer C. T1 seeds retransmissions, 64 times T1 ends the transaction, and Timer C is the proxy's longer INVITE arm.
docs.eg: Count the gaps The second and third arrows are retransmissions. State the first Timer A value.

docs.ex: Transactions and the branch cookie. A transaction is identified by the branch, and a retransmission repeats that branch instead of starting a new one.
docs.eg: Compare the two branches Inspect the retransmitted INVITE and the ACK. Decide which hop starts a new transaction.

docs.ex: UDP, TCP, TLS, and WebSocket. The transport is a property of the hop, written in Via, and it changes retransmission and framing rather than the SIP methods.
docs.eg: Read the teaching config The config is a dial-peer, a trusted source, an empty profile, and one debug command.

docs.ex: CANCEL, BYE, and re-INVITE. CANCEL abandons an unanswered INVITE, BYE ends a confirmed dialog, and re-INVITE changes a dialog that already exists.
docs.eg: Dissect a BYE This BYE assumes the dialog already exists. Find the CSeq and the To tag.

docs.ex: PRACK and reliable provisionals. A provisional response with Require: 100rel is retransmitted until PRACK, and RAck names that exact response.
docs.eg: Check RAck Dissect the PRACK. Separate RAck from CSeq.

docs.ex: Record-Route and the route set. A proxy that wants to stay on the dialog prepends a Record-Route URI, and that URI has to contain lr.
docs.eg: Put lr back The header-rule matches a Record-Route that lost lr and writes the parameter back.

docs.ex: REFER and Replaces. REFER asks another UA to send a request, and Replaces names the dialog that request should take over.
docs.eg: Read Refer-To Find the Replaces parameter inside Refer-To. It is escaped.

docs.ex: Session-Expires and 422. Session timers name who refreshes the dialog, and 422 tells the caller the interval was below Min-SE.
docs.eg: Read the 422 The response tells you the floor. The next INVITE has to meet it.

docs.ex: Two different ACK rules. The ACK for a non-2xx is hop by hop inside the INVITE transaction, and the ACK for a 2xx is a new end-to-end transaction.
docs.eg: Whose branch is on the ACK? Inspect both ACKs. Each one repeats the branch of the INVITE on that hop.

docs.ex: UPDATE before the INVITE completes. UPDATE can change the session while the initial INVITE is still outstanding, and it does not use the ACK rules.
docs.eg: Negotiate the second offer The UPDATE offer adds a port change and still lists PCMU and PCMA. The answer keeps PCMU.

docs.ex: Locating a server with RFC 3263. RFC 3263 turns a SIP domain into a transport, a port, and an address with NAPTR, SRV, and A or AAAA.
docs.eg: What happened before the INVITE The first note states the DNS result. The SIP itself contains no NAPTR records.

docs.ex: Forking and early dialogs. A forking proxy creates one client transaction per binding, and each To tag is a separate early dialog.
docs.eg: Separate the tags Step both 180 responses. The Call-ID matches and the To tags do not.

docs.ex: GRUU and a single instance. A GRUU routes to one UA instance, and the registrar returns it as pub-gruu or temp-gruu on the binding.
docs.eg: Find both GRUUs The 200 OK Contact carries pub-gruu and temp-gruu.

docs.ex: Loose routing and Max-Forwards. With lr, the Request-URI stays the remote target, each hop pops its own Route, and Max-Forwards of 0 yields 483.
docs.eg: Watch Route shrink Compare the Route headers on the first and second BYE.

docs.ex: Outbound, reg-id, and keepalives. RFC 5626 binds a UA instance to one or more flows with reg-id and +sip.instance, and keepalives hold those flows open.
docs.eg: Count the flows Dissect the second 200 OK. Two Contact headers share an instance and differ by reg-id.

docs.ex: Path and Service-Route. Path is the inbound vector stored with a binding, and Service-Route is the outbound vector the registrar gives the UA.
docs.eg: Which header is outbound? The 200 OK has both Path and Service-Route. Pick the one the UA will preload.

docs.ex: REGISTER and bindings. REGISTER binds an address-of-record to one or more Contacts, and the registrar is a different role from the proxy.
docs.eg: Read the 423 The registrar rejected the interval. The header you need is Min-Expires.

docs.ex: Direction attributes and hold. sendrecv, sendonly, recvonly, and inactive are per stream. Hold is commonly sendonly or inactive.
docs.eg: Answer a hold The offer is sendonly. A legal answer is recvonly. Negotiate and read the direction line.

docs.ex: Early media and 183. 183 Session Progress with SDP is the usual early-media pattern. 180 means ringing. A 183 does not always have SDP.
docs.eg: 183 has SDP, 180 does not Extract both responses. One progress message has SDP and the ringing message does not.

docs.ex: Same m-lines, same order. RFC 3264 matches streams by position. The answer has the same number of m-lines, in the same order.
docs.eg: Negotiate two m-lines Run the negotiator. The answer refuses the second stream without deleting it.

docs.ex: Offer/answer pitfalls in RFC 6337. RFC 6337 is the usage document for offer/answer mistakes: order, version, delayed offer, and hold.
docs.eg: Find the delayed offer This INVITE has an empty body. Decide where the offer is allowed to appear.

docs.ex: Port 0 rejects a stream. Port 0 refuses the stream in that slot. The m-line stays, with a protocol and a format list.
docs.eg: See a zero port Negotiate an offer of two audio lines. The answer accepts the first and zeros the second.

docs.ex: rtpmap names and fmtp parameters. Match codecs by the rtpmap encoding name. The G.722 rtpmap clock stays 8000.
docs.eg: Match opus on the name The offer says payload 96 opus. The answer says payload 111 opus. G722/8000 is on payload 9 on both sides.

docs.ti: The lines in an SDP body
docs.ex: The lines in an SDP body. Read v, o, s, c, t, m, and a lines as a session description. RFC 8866 is the current SDP specification.
docs.eg: Point at c= and m= Dissect the INVITE and find the connection line and both media lines.

docs.ex: G.711, G.729, and Opus. Choose a codec both sides named. Read RFC 6716 and the Opus license before you draw any legal conclusion.
docs.eg: See opus survive a new payload type Negotiate the offer and answer. Confirm opus matches across payload types 96 and 111, and that G722 stays at 8000.

docs.ex: One-way audio. A 200 OK can be perfect while one RTP direction is missing. Read direction, c=, and who is actually sending.
docs.eg: Spot sendonly in the answer Extract the INVITE and the 200 OK. Compare a=sendrecv in the offer with the answer direction.

docs.ex: Static and dynamic payload types. RFC 3551 assigns static payload types. Dynamic types are named by rtpmap, and G.722 stays at clock 8000.
docs.eg: Read static types The offer lists PCMU and PCMA on separate m-lines. Confirm the clocks are 8000.

docs.ex: ptime, packet rate, and EF. ptime is SDP. Twenty milliseconds of G.711 is 50 packets per second and 160 bytes of payload, plus headers. Voice sits in the EF class.
docs.eg: Read ptime 20 Both sides show a=ptime:20 and PCMU/8000. Compute packets per second and payload bytes.

docs.ex: RTCP sender and receiver reports. RTCP sender reports and receiver reports describe the RTP flow. A SIP 200 OK does not report loss.
docs.eg: Name the RTCP port The answer says m=audio 40030. Apply the RFC 3550 default and name the RTCP port.

docs.ex: The RTP header. RTP version 2 carries a sequence number, a timestamp, an SSRC, and a marker bit. SIP does not carry those fields.
docs.eg: Find where the header is not Dissect the 200 OK. The body names a port. The RTP header is not one of the SIP headers.

docs.ex: telephone-event and other digit paths. telephone-event is RFC 4733, a dynamic payload. Events 0 through 15 are DTMF. INFO and KPML are different tools.
docs.eg: Negotiate telephone-event The offer uses payload 101 and the answer uses payload 106. Both rtpmap lines say telephone-event/8000 and fmtp lists 0-15.

docs.ex: 401, 407, and digest. A 401 from a UAS is answered with Authorization. A 407 from a proxy is answered with Proxy-Authorization.
docs.eg: Read a 407 Dissect the 407. Name the challenge header and the header the client must send next.

docs.ex: Hardening a SIP edge. A defensive edge limits peers, requires digest and TLS, strips PAI, and does not share SRTP keying across legs.
docs.eg: Checklist, not a device stanza Read the teaching checklist. It is not a vendor configuration and it is not a router QoS policy.

docs.ex: Privacy and asserted identity. Privacy is RFC 3323. P-Asserted-Identity and P-Preferred-Identity are for trusted networks, not cryptographic identity.
docs.eg: See PAI on the wrong hop This INVITE is addressed to the carrier and still contains P-Asserted-Identity and Privacy: id.

docs.ex: SRTP and two keying methods. SRTP is RFC 3711. SDES a=crypto is RFC 4568. DTLS-SRTP is RFC 5764. An SBC must not assume peers share one method.
docs.eg: See the profile mismatch The offer is RTP/SAVP. The answer is RTP/AVP. Negotiate and read the profile warning.

docs.ex: STIR, PASSporT, and SHAKEN. STIR is RFC 8224, PASSporT is RFC 8225, certificates are RFC 8226, and the SHAKEN extension is RFC 8588. Attestation levels are ATIS.
docs.eg: No Identity header Dissect the INVITE. Decide whether it is STIR-authenticated.

docs.ex: Scanning, hijack, and toll fraud. Scanning, registration hijack, and toll fraud are classes of abuse. The response is authentication, exposure control, and alerting.
docs.eg: Read an unchallenged REGISTER result Dissect the 200 OK. The Contact is 192.0.2.40 and there was no digest challenge.

docs.ex: TLS and domain certificates. SIP over TLS is RFC 3261 section 18. The certificate has to identify the SIP domain, per RFC 5922.
docs.eg: Read a TLS Via Dissect the INVITE. The transport is TLS. The domain in the request is example.com.

docs.ex: ICE candidate types. ICE is RFC 8445, which obsoletes RFC 5245. Candidates are host, srflx, prflx, and relay.
docs.eg: Read the candidate types Negotiate the offer. Then read the a=candidate lines yourself. The negotiator matches codecs. You match the types.

docs.ex: Media latching on an SBC. Many SBCs learn the remote RTP address from the first packet instead of trusting c=. That is deployment practice, and RFC 5853 is the requirements RFC.
docs.eg: Compare c= with the packet source Extract the INVITE and read c=. Then read the RTP note. The source port's address is not the c= address.

docs.ex: Embedded addresses and NAT. SIP and SDP embed IP addresses. NAT rewrites the packet header and leaves those embedded addresses behind.
docs.eg: Read a routable c= line Dissect the offer. c= uses the documentation address 203.0.113.10. The fault beside this lab is the private-address case.

docs.ex: rport and symmetric responses. RFC 3581 adds rport so the response is sent to the source address and port the request came from.
docs.eg: Read rport on the response Dissect the 100 Trying. Via has received and rport filled in.

docs.ex: The SIP ALG problem. A SIP ALG rewrites SIP and SDP in transit and often corrupts the call. It cannot rewrite TLS.
docs.eg: See a stale length Dissect the forwarded INVITE. Content-Length does not match the body.

docs.ex: STUN server-reflexive addresses. STUN, RFC 8489, lets a client learn the address a server sees. It obsoletes RFC 5389.
docs.eg: Separate STUN text from SIP The capture has a STUN note and a SIP 200 OK. Only one of them is a Binding result.

docs.ex: TURN relays. TURN, RFC 8656, allocates a relay when host and server-reflexive paths fail. It obsoletes RFC 5766.
docs.eg: Read an Allocate result The text is a TURN result, not a SIP request. Identify the relayed address.

docs.ti: Call admission stays on the datasheet
docs.ex: Call admission stays on the datasheet. An SBC can refuse a new INVITE when its configured budget is exhausted. The number itself is platform-specific.
docs.eg: Read the refusal Step the ladder. Which response refuses the call?

docs.ti: An SBC is commonly a B2BUA
docs.ex: An SBC is commonly a B2BUA. RFC 7092 taxonomizes B2BUAs. An SBC is commonly a UAS on one side and a UAC on the other, not a pure proxy.
docs.eg: Dissect the outbound INVITE This is the SBC’s outbound INVITE. Which Call-ID belongs to the carrier leg?

docs.ti: Active and standby, without a made-up timer
docs.ex: Active and standby, without a made-up timer. Active/standby is a product behavior. One unit owns the work and the other is ready. Timers belong in that product’s HA guide.
docs.eg: Count the SIP hops Play the call. How many SIP roles does the standby occupy in the ladder?

docs.ex: Anchor, bypass, transcode, and DTMF. Anchoring terminates RTP on the SBC. Bypass lets endpoints exchange media. Transcoding and DTMF interworking need the media path.
docs.eg: Negotiate an anchored answer Alice offers PCMU and PCMA. The anchored answer keeps PCMU and telephone-event.

docs.ex: OPTIONS keepalives. SBCs probe a peer with OPTIONS. A 200 OK means the peer answered. The interval is product configuration.
docs.eg: Check the OPTIONS CSeq Dissect this keepalive. What is the CSeq method?

docs.ti: RFC 5853 is requirements, not a protocol
docs.ex: RFC 5853 is requirements, not a protocol. RFC 5853 collects requirements from SBC deployments. It does not define an SBC wire protocol.
docs.eg: Find the protocol Play the ladder. Which start line is an SBC-specific method?

docs.ti: Topology hiding rewrites the addresses you leak
docs.ex: Topology hiding rewrites the addresses you leak. Topology hiding replaces caller addresses in signaling and, when media is anchored, in SDP.
docs.eg: Compare Contact hosts Dissect the carrier INVITE. Which host is in Contact?

docs.ti: CUBE is an IOS XE B2BUA
docs.ex: CUBE is an IOS XE B2BUA. Cisco Unified Border Element is a B2BUA on IOS XE. It shares the IOS voice stack with other voice features.
docs.eg: Walk a CUBE call Play the ladder and name the B2BUA hop.

docs.ti: CUCM trunks, SIP profiles, and Lua
docs.ex: CUCM trunks, SIP profiles, and Lua. A CUCM SIP trunk and a CUCM SIP profile are not the CUBE voice class. Lua normalization scripts exist. MTP required is version-specific.
docs.eg: Dissect the trunk INVITE This INVITE leaves CUCM toward CUBE. Which host is in Contact?

docs.ex: debug ccsip messages. debug ccsip messages displays sent and received SIP. Profile decisions have a separate debug, and the analyzer can test a profile offline.
docs.eg: Parse a synthetic debug This is synthetic debug ccsip messages output. Separate Received from Sent.

docs.ti: Dial peers select the SIP next hop
docs.ex: Dial peers select the SIP next hop. dial-peer voice N voip, session protocol sipv2, and session target ipv4: name a SIP next hop.
docs.eg: Read dial peer 200 This is the carrier dial peer. Where will CUBE send the outbound INVITE?

docs.ex: Early offer and delayed offer. Delayed offer means the INVITE has no SDP. voice-class sip early-offer forced makes the outbound dial peer send an offer in the INVITE.
docs.eg: Read the forced offer The outbound early offer is ANCHOR_SDP. The carrier answer is CARRIER_SDP.

docs.ex: voice class sip-profiles. A voice class sip-profiles rule can add, modify, or remove a header on a named method. Inbound support arrived after Cisco IOS 15.4.
docs.eg: Remove Diversion Run the CUBE subset rule against the inbound INVITE. Diversion should disappear.

docs.ex: Unity Connection SIP integration. SIP integration with CUCM is the documented Unity Connection path. Open the guide for your version. This lesson does not make SCCP the default.
docs.eg: Find the called number Dissect the forwarded INVITE. Which header carries +15551212 as the redirecting target?

docs.ex: Header rules run in order. Oracle HMR header rules run in configured order. The 10.1 fundamentals page names add, delete, manipulate, store, and reject.
docs.eg: Delete Server Run this Acme header-rule subset against the INVITE. Server should disappear.

docs.ex: AudioCodes manipulation in software 7.6. Software 7.6 message manipulation is a table of Message Type, Condition, Action Subject, Action Type, and Action Value, assigned to an IP group.
docs.eg: Read one 7.6 row Which column contains Remove?

docs.ex: Certificate names and Contact. The certificate name and the SIP Contact need to be names the peer accepts. Teams and Webex Local Gateway do not share a wildcard rule.
docs.eg: Read the Teams Contact Dissect the TLS INVITE. Is Contact an FQDN or an IP?

docs.ex: Three manipulation grammars. CUBE, Oracle HMR, and AudioCodes 7.6 can each remove a header. The grammars are not interchangeable.
docs.eg: Identify the row Three fragments are printed. Which one is the AudioCodes 7.6 action?

docs.ex: Oracle SBC objects. Oracle Communications SBC, formerly Acme Packet, is configured with realms, interfaces, session agents, and manipulation objects.
docs.eg: Name the attachment These are documentation object names. Which one selects manipulation for messages leaving?

docs.ex: Identity at a trust boundary. P-Asserted-Identity is a network-asserted identity. An SBC at a trust boundary decides whether that assertion continues.
docs.eg: Find the assertion Dissect the carrier INVITE. Which header asserts the identity?

docs.ti: Ribbon Edge, Core, and public validation lists
docs.ex: Ribbon Edge, Core, and public validation lists. SBC SWe Edge shares a software family with SBC 1000 and SBC 2000. SBC Core is a separate family. Admin guides and interop guides are the sources for procedures.
docs.eg: Keep the families apart Play the call. Which SIP method names the Ribbon family?

docs.ex: Amazon Connect voice boundaries. Ordinary Connect calls use managed PSTN. SIPREC can feed a conversational analytics connector. A carrier bridged through Voice Connector is not the supported pattern.
docs.eg: Name the recording relationship Dissect the synthetic SIPREC INVITE. Which address is the Request-URI host?

docs.ti: Five9 BYO SIP and Twilio trunks
docs.ex: Five9 BYO SIP and Twilio trunks. Five9 BYO SIP connects your ITSP or gateway to Five9 SBCs. Twilio termination and origination are different directions, with a strict Request-URI rule.
docs.eg: Read the termination Request-URI The termination URI host in this lab is sbc1.example.com. What host does this INVITE use?

docs.ti: Genesys BYOC and NICE CXone SIP
docs.ex: Genesys BYOC and NICE CXone SIP. BYOC Cloud and BYOC Premises can be combined. NICE CXone documents SIP trunks on 5060 and 5061 with dynamic RTP and SRTP. Confirm carrier details with NICE.
docs.eg: Whose date is it? Play the BYOC Cloud ladder, then answer from the Premises article rather than from the SIP itself.

docs.ex: OPTIONS health and SRTP media. OPTIONS followed by 200 marks the SBC healthy. Media processors use SRTP. The protocol article’s OPTIONS CSeq cell disagrees with RFC 3261.
docs.eg: Dissect a legal OPTIONS This is the request to send. What is the CSeq method?

docs.ex: Teams Direct Routing signaling. Direct Routing uses the pstnhub proxies on 5061, a certified SBC, and a verified domain. Contact must be an FQDN.
docs.eg: Check Contact and the proxy host Dissect the Direct Routing INVITE. Which host is in Contact?

docs.ex: Webex Calling Local Gateway. An IOS XE Local Gateway uses SIP TLS and SRTP. Third-party SBCs use a certificate-based trunk. Wildcard certificates are not supported. ByoPSTN means bring your own PSTN.
docs.eg: Read the Local Gateway offer The Local Gateway offer is SRTP. Which transport is in the m= line?

docs.ti: Three PSTN choices, one per location
docs.ex: Three PSTN choices, one per location. Webex Calling offers Cisco Calling Plan, Cloud Connected PSTN, or premises-based PSTN through a Local Gateway. A location has one PSTN connection.
docs.eg: Name this ladder Step the call. Which PSTN model is on the wire here?

docs.ti: Read an RFC header before you cite it
docs.ex: Read an RFC header before you cite it. Number, category, and Obsoletes or Updates. The RFC Editor header beats a remembered month.
docs.eg: Name the SDP RFC on the offer Inspect the first INVITE body. Which RFC number does this lesson use for SDP now?

docs.ex: IOS ccsip and ccapi debug. debug ccsip messages prints SIP on IOS voice. debug voip ccapi inout prints call-control API output, which is not a SIP RFC.
docs.eg: Dissect the SIP inside the debug The message below is what a synthetic debug ccsip messages capture would contain after the IOS prefix. debug voip ccapi inout is a different IOS command and is not this text.

docs.ex: 488 codecs and 422 session timers. 488 is this UA refusing the session description. 422 is a session interval below Min-SE.
docs.eg: See the overlap Negotiate this synthetic offer and answer. PCMU and telephone-event are on both sides. PCMA is only in the offer.

docs.ti: Match a ladder before you change anything
docs.ex: Match a ladder before you change anything. A ladder is one dialog only after Call-ID, CSeq, the Via branch, and the To tag agree.
docs.eg: Find the end-to-end ACK Play the ladder. Which hop is the ACK for the 200 OK, and which branch does it use?

docs.ti: Status codes you will actually see
docs.ex: Status codes you will actually see. Read provisional and final codes from RFC 3261 section 21, and keep 422 with RFC 4028.
docs.eg: Name the 487 Step the ladder. Which response ends the INVITE, and which 200 belongs to the CANCEL?

docs.ti: TLS names, trust anchors, and version
docs.ex: TLS names, trust anchors, and version. Handshake failures stay below SIP. A Teams 403 is the Contact FQDN rule after TLS is up.
docs.eg: Find the FQDN Inspect the INVITE Contact. What hostname is in it, and what would a bare address draw?

docs.ti: Display filters for SIP and RTP
docs.ex: Display filters for SIP and RTP. Filter the capture with sip, rtp, and sip.Method, and confirm sip.CSeq.method in the SIP display-filter reference.
docs.eg: Extract the INVITE from a text capture This is a synthetic text capture, not a customer packet. Extract the SIP message. On a real file you would display-filter with sip, and you would confirm sip.CSeq.method == "INVITE" in the Wireshark SIP display-filter reference.

docs.ex: Alarms that match the failure. Alarm on OPTIONS, TLS expiry, 503, recording-session failure, and trusted-list rejects. Each alarm names its document.
docs.eg: Read the 503 What status did the carrier return to OPTIONS, and what class of alarm is it?

docs.ex: One change in the window. Freeze the baseline, change one variable, verify, and keep the previous snippet ready.
docs.eg: Count the variables Between the baseline OPTIONS and the INVITE, how many variables did the lesson change?

docs.ti: Emergency calling, location, and the FCC page
docs.ex: Emergency calling, location, and the FCC page. Service URN, location conveyance, and the FCC MLTS page. State PSAP rules are not invented here.
docs.eg: Read the Request-URI Inspect the first INVITE. What is the Request-URI?

docs.ex: The toll-fraud class, stated defensively. Four exposure classes, source restrictions, and caller-identity as a separate control.
docs.eg: Name the listed source Which source address on the first hop is the listed call agent?

docs.ti: Voice, EF, and what the PHB does not design
docs.ex: Voice, EF, and what the PHB does not design. RFC 3246 defines the EF PHB. RFC 4594 maps telephony to EF. This lesson does not design a LAN.
docs.eg: Where EF applies Which hop's SDP names the media that the telephony class covers?

docs.ex: Disclosed recording with SIPREC. RFC 7866 is the recording protocol. RFC 7865 is the metadata. Notice and retention are legal questions.
docs.eg: Separate the two Call-IDs Which Call-ID belongs to the recording session toward the SRS?

docs.ex: Trusted addresses and source restrictions. The IP address trusted list is per product page. CME and SRST do not share one list size.
docs.eg: Trusted list teaching snippet Read the snippet. It is the CME pattern for a border that trusts the call agent and the carrier. SRST uses its own page. No list size is stated.

docs.ex: Certifications this edition will name. SSCA, CCNP Collaboration, and MS-721, with the dates this edition actually checked. Other vendor exam codes stay unconfirmed.
docs.eg: Cite the ACK the exams share The last hop is the ACK for 200 OK. Which documents cover it?

docs.ti: Webex Calling local gateway, and a separate contact center
docs.ex: Webex Calling local gateway, and a separate contact center. Premises PSTN for Webex Calling uses Local Gateway. Webex Contact Center is a separate product with its own design guide.
docs.eg: Name the pattern Which product's premises-PSTN pattern is this ladder?

docs.ti: A glossary tied to a document
docs.ex: A glossary tied to a document. Every term in your notes points at a role and a document, not at a product logo.
docs.eg: Name the outbound role On the outbound INVITE, which role do you write if this SBC is a B2BUA?

docs.ti: Neighbors that are not SIP elements
docs.ex: Neighbors that are not SIP elements. WFM and QM are operations systems. CRM is not a SIP element. Recording, location, and the media path keep their real documents.
docs.eg: Keep CRM off the arrow Which party list would wrongly add a CRM as a SIP hop?

docs.ti: When the page and the memory disagree
docs.ex: When the page and the memory disagree. The RFC Editor banner, the Cisco exam page, and the Microsoft certification page outrank a remembered line.
docs.eg: Who wins on SDP The offer is SDP. Which number do you cite when a blog still says 4566 is current?

docs.ti: CUCM, UCCX, and CVP without a fake script
docs.ex: CUCM, UCCX, and CVP without a fake script. CUCM is the call-control point. UCCX rides on CUCM. CVP's SIP paths are in the guide for the version you run.
docs.eg: Where the carrier INVITE stops first The first hop is the carrier. Which element receives it?

docs.ti: Workforce tools and agents above the media
docs.ex: Workforce tools and agents above the media. Agents and workforce tools sit above the media path. The session is still SIP, and the voice is still RTP.
docs.eg: Point at the media hop Which response carries the answer that lets RTP start?

docs.ti: An interconnect checklist, not a config dump
docs.ex: An interconnect checklist, not a config dump. Record TLS, codecs including telephone-event, E.164, trusted addresses, OPTIONS, and the SRTP keying choice.
docs.eg: Find two rows on the INVITE The INVITE hop carries a number and an offer. Which checklist rows are those?

docs.ti: CUCM, a certified SBC, and Teams Direct Routing
docs.ex: CUCM, a certified SBC, and Teams Direct Routing. CUBE or another certified SBC can sit between CUCM and Teams. No architecture SKU is invented here.
docs.eg: Read Contact on the Teams INVITE What does Contact contain on the hop toward Teams?

docs.ti: Media drill with the cited answer
docs.ex: Media drill with the cited answer. 488, 422, telephone-event, RTP, and the SRTP keying choice, each answered in the prose.
docs.eg: Name this 488 The final response is 488. What do you say in the interview?

docs.ti: SBC drill with the cited answer
docs.ex: SBC drill with the cited answer. B2BUA, where PSTN SIP lands, the trusted list, and Teams TLS, answered in the body.
docs.eg: Count the legs How do you match the carrier 200 to the caller's ACK?

docs.ti: Signaling drill with the cited answer
docs.ex: Signaling drill with the cited answer. Each signaling answer is written here, with the RFC, before the quiz asks it.
docs.eg: Say the ACK kind The last hop follows 200 OK. What kind of ACK is it?

docs.ti: Symptom, ladder, one packet, one variable
docs.ex: Symptom, ladder, one packet, one variable. The sequence is symptom, ladder, one packet, change one variable. The log in this lesson is synthetic.
docs.eg: Pick the one packet Which hop is the packet the method allows you to act on before you change config?

docs.ex: When the RFC number moves. SDP, ICE, STUN, and TURN moved. The RFC Editor banner beats a blog, and an uncited successor stays an open question.
docs.eg: Cite the offer The first INVITE carries SDP. Which number is current in this library?

docs.ex: Browser softphone call flow. A study ladder: WebSocket handshake, SIP INVITE, answer, then DTLS on the media path. Step the hops.
docs.eg: Step the softphone ladder Play or step. Stop on DTLS and say which path it uses.

docs.ti: DTLS-SRTP and the required audio codecs
docs.ex: DTLS-SRTP and the required audio codecs. WebRTC media is SRTP. The profile is RTP/SAVPF. Opus, PCMA, and PCMU are required audio codecs.
docs.eg: Read the offer proto and the Opus line The offer uses UDP/TLS/RTP/SAVPF and names opus/48000/2. The answer keeps Opus.

docs.ex: ICE, STUN, and TURN. ICE gathers host, server-reflexive, and relayed candidates. STUN and TURN are the tools. The default STUN port is 3478.
docs.eg: Sort the candidates Three lines from a study checklist. Match each one to the RFC 8445 name.

docs.ti: Signaling, JSEP, and the media plane
docs.ex: Signaling, JSEP, and the media plane. WebRTC names a browser protocol suite. JSEP leaves the signaling protocol to the application. SIP over WebSocket is one such protocol.
docs.eg: Name the document Step the ladder. The first hop is an HTTP handshake. The third hop is SIP.

docs.ex: RFC 7118: the sip subprotocol. The handshake must offer sip. Via uses WS or WSS. The URI transport parameter added by the RFC is ws.
docs.eg: Read the REGISTER This synthetic REGISTER uses a .invalid host, Via WSS, and transport=ws. It is a study message, not a copy of the RFC example.

docs.ex: Asterisk, PJSIP, and the dialplan. chan_pjsip is the SIP channel driver. res_pjsip reads pjsip.conf. extensions.conf is the dialplan. The license page is GPL version 2, with a stated exception for AMI, AGI, and ARI.
docs.eg: Which file A study sketch with the file names from the docs. It is not a working endpoint.

docs.ex: Four projects, four roles. Read the role each project states. Do not treat them as four names for one PBX.
docs.eg: Place the box Four lines. Pick the one that proxies RTP.

docs.ex: FreeSWITCH profiles, dialplan, and WebRTC. The manual covers SIP profiles, the dialplan, codecs, media, WebRTC, and the Event Socket. There is an open source edition and an enterprise edition.
docs.eg: Separate the products Three names from the page. Pick the open source build.

docs.ex: Kamailio as the SIP server. Kamailio is an open source SIP server under GPLv2+. Its page lists proxy, registrar, WebSocket, and scaling in front of a PBX.
docs.eg: Who answers the dialplan Kamailio received the INVITE. Asterisk is the next hop.

docs.ex: rtpengine and the integration map. rtpengine proxies RTP, rewrites SDP, and can bridge ICE and SRTP. It runs on GNU/Linux and is meant to sit with Kamailio.
docs.eg: Read the rewritten c= line The offer points at the phone. The answer points at the proxy. That is the anchoring idea.

docs.ex: Troubleshooting without a legal conclusion. Sort the symptom into SIP, identity, emergency location, or messaging. Then open that document. Educational only. Not legal advice.
docs.eg: Pick the next document One symptom. One next document. No legal conclusion.

docs.ti: Kari's Law, RAY BAUM'S Act, and SIP location
docs.ex: Kari's Law, RAY BAUM'S Act, and SIP location. Public Law 115-127 requires direct 911 dialing from MLTS. Section 506 of RAY BAUM'S Act requires a proceeding on dispatchable location. Educational only. Not legal advice.
docs.eg: Which document Match the duty to the text. This is not a determination about a building.

docs.ti: How to read a compliance page
docs.ex: How to read a compliance page. This lesson is educational. It is not legal advice, not a compliance opinion, and not a filing. Statutes and the FCC pages outrank this lab. A quiz answer is not a legal conclusion.
docs.eg: Classify the document Three opened sources. Match the topic.

docs.ex: STIR and SHAKEN. RFC 8224 defines a signed SIP Identity header. RFC 8225 defines PASSporT. SHAKEN is the industry mechanism the ATIS STI-GA page describes. Educational only.
docs.eg: Find the header The Identity value is a placeholder. Do not treat it as a signature.

docs.ex: 10DLC is a messaging channel. The Campaign Registry describes 10DLC as an A2P messaging channel with verified brands and campaign service providers. It is not SIP. Educational only.
docs.eg: Split the ticket Two symptoms arrived in one ticket. Separate them.

docs.ti: Bridges from enterprise UC to open platforms
docs.ex: Bridges from enterprise UC to open platforms. CUCM, Webex, and the contact center already have SIP seams in this lab. The open projects are the other side of a trunk, not a hidden mode inside CUCM.
docs.eg: Name both sides A trunk is up. Name the object on each side without merging the names.

docs.ex: Configuration and troubleshooting seams. Configure the file the project names. Troubleshoot the plane that failed. Do not copy a sample this lab did not print.
docs.eg: Choose the file The endpoint exists. The extension 1000 does not ring. Asterisk is the PBX.

docs.ti: Integration hooks that are already named
docs.ex: Integration hooks that are already named. Future work should use hooks the documents already name: AMI, AGI, ARI, the Event Socket, SIPREC, and SIP over WebSocket. This lab does not ship a live connector.
docs.eg: Pick a real hook You want a program to hear that an Asterisk call is ringing. Choose an interface the license page names.

docs.ex: Glossary and the mind map. The glossary is a short definition plus a citation. The mind map is a topic picture, not a network diagram.
docs.eg: Pick the citation Three terms. One citation each. Do not add a fourth from memory.

docs.ex: Sister technologies around the session. WFM, recording, emergency policy, analytics, CRM, AI agents, and programmable APIs hang off the session. They are not SIP proxies.
docs.eg: Name the neighbor The symptom is a recording that never starts. SIP to the phone works.

Cheat codes. 16 sheets. Each one carries the disclaimer, the three lab links, and sources.
Help. Menu is the top-left button. On a phone it is also the left side of the bottom bar: Menu, Learn, Diagrams, Play, Listen, Guide. Escape, Close, or a tap outside puts the drawer away.
Play. Port match uses the rows on Ports . A high score is not a certification.
Glossary. Session Initiation Protocol. Application signaling that creates, modifies, and ends sessions.
SIP Universe Free University. Download cheat codes Open the benches
Animated flows. 140 drawings move a packet along the message. Reduced motion in Settings stops extra page motion. The SVG animation is in the file.
Ports and protocols. Well-known SIP ports come from the RFCs and IANA. Cloud ranges below were read from the vendor page on the date in this file. If a vendor edits the page, the page wins.
